title: Learning from Failure: A Simulated Case Study of an Adult Education Centre
instructions: 阅读下面的文章，回答10个问题。文章是关于一个成人教育中心如何从失败中学习的模拟案例。请先通读全文，再做题。题目类型包括单选、填空、匹配和判断正误/未提及。填空答案必须来自原文，且不超过字数限制。所有题目和选项均为英文，解释为中文。
passage:
A. In 2022, the Westbridge Adult Education Centre launched a new evening course called 'Digital Skills for Work'. The centre expected 40 students, but only 12 enrolled. The course ran for eight weeks, and by the end, only five students were still attending. This was a serious problem, because low enrolment and poor attendance meant the course was not achieving its purpose of helping adults improve their digital skills for employment. The centre's director, Maria Chen, was disappointed. She called a meeting with the course teacher, David Kim, and the administrator, Sarah Patel. They wanted to understand why the course had failed, rather than simply accepting the poor result. This decision to investigate rather than ignore the problem was the first step towards improvement.

B. At the meeting, David said, 'The main problem was the time. Many students told me they finished work at 6 p.m. and could not get to the centre by 6:30. The course started too early.' This comment pointed to a practical scheduling issue: students needed enough time to travel from their workplaces to the centre. Sarah added, 'We also advertised the course only on our website. Most of our students don't check the website often. They use social media.' Her point suggested that the centre had used the wrong communication channel to reach its audience. Maria listened and took notes. She said, 'So we need a later start time and better advertising. But let's not guess. Let's collect evidence.' Her response showed the importance of testing assumptions rather than acting on opinion alone, and it set the direction for the team's next steps.

C. The team decided to gather data. They sent a short survey to all 12 students who enrolled. Seven students replied, which gave the team a reasonable amount of feedback to work with. The survey asked: Why did you leave? What time would suit you better? How did you hear about the course? The answers showed that five students left because of the time, and two left because they found the course too difficult. This revealed two separate problems: scheduling and the level of difficulty. The survey also showed that most students heard about the course from a friend, not from the website. This supported Sarah's earlier point about advertising and confirmed that word of mouth was a powerful channel the centre had not been using.

D. Maria also looked at the enrolment numbers for other courses. She noticed that courses starting at 7 p.m. had higher attendance than those starting at 6:30. She shared this with the team. 'This is useful evidence,' she said. 'It suggests that a later start time could help. But we need to test it.' By comparing different courses, Maria was able to identify a pattern that supported the survey findings. However, she understood that evidence alone does not prove a solution will work; it must be tested in practice. This cautious approach prevented the team from making changes based on a single source of information.

E. The team made two changes for the next course. First, they moved the start time to 7 p.m. Second, they advertised on social media and asked current students to tell their friends. They also added a short 'taster' session before the course began, so students could try before enrolling. This gave potential students a chance to experience the course and decide whether it suited them. The new course started in January 2023. This time, 28 students enrolled, and 22 completed the course. The completion rate was much higher, which suggested that the changes had made a positive difference and that the evidence-based approach had been worthwhile.

F. However, not everything improved. The teacher, David, reported that some students still found the material too difficult. 'The taster session helped, but we need to check students' levels before they join,' he said. Maria agreed. 'We learned that collecting evidence is important, but we also need to act on it quickly. Next time, we will ask students about their level before the course starts.' This showed that improvement is an ongoing process, and that solving one problem can reveal another. The team accepted this as a natural part of learning rather than a new failure.

G. The centre now has a simple rule: after every course, they hold a short 'learning review'. They ask three questions: What worked? What didn't work? What will we change? They write down the answers and share them with all teachers. This routine helps the organisation turn experience into shared knowledge, so that lessons learned in one course benefit future courses and other teachers. Maria says, 'Failure is not the end. It is information. If we use it well, we can improve.'

H. This case shows how an organisation can learn from failure. It is not enough to feel bad about a bad result. You need to find out why it happened, collect evidence, make changes, and then check if the changes worked. The Westbridge Centre did this, and their courses are now more successful. Their experience demonstrates that failure can be valuable when it is treated as a source of information rather than simply as a setback, and that a systematic approach to learning from mistakes can turn a disappointing outcome into lasting improvement.

questions.evidence: The main problem was the time. Many students told me they finished work at 6 p.m. and could not get to the centre by 6:30. The course started too early.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence with ONE WORD from the passage: The team sent a short ______ to all 12 students who enrolled.

questions.evidence: The survey also showed that most students heard about the course from a friend, not from the website.

grammar.title: 一般过去时与现在完成时的区别（重点复查高频错误）
grammar.explanation: 在英语中，一般过去时表示过去某个具体时间发生的动作或状态，常与明确的时间状语连用，如 in 2022, last week, yesterday。现在完成时表示过去发生的动作对现在造成的影响或结果，或者从过去持续到现在的状态，常与 already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for 等连用。注意：现在完成时不能与表示具体过去时间的状语连用。例如：We launched the course in 2022.（正确）We have launched the course in 2022.（错误）
grammar.example: The course ran for eight weeks, and by the end, only five students were still attending.

options: She has finished her report yesterday.
She has finish her report yesterday.
questions.explanation: yesterday 是具体过去时间，必须用一般过去时 finished。现在完成时不能与 yesterday 连用。

options: I have seen that film last week.
I saw that film last week.
I have saw that film last week.
I see that film last week.
answers: I saw that film last week.
questions.explanation: last week 是具体过去时间，用一般过去时 saw。
questions.evidence: I saw that film last week.

options: They have already left the office.
They have already leave the office.
They has already left the office.
answers: They have already left the office.
questions.explanation: already 常与现在完成时连用，表示动作已完成，对现在有影响。主语 They 用 have。
questions.evidence: They have already left the office.

questions.explanation: since 2010 表示从过去持续到现在，用现在完成时 has lived。

options: We have visited the museum two days ago.
We visited the museum two days ago.
We have visit the museum two days ago.
We visit the museum two days ago.
answers: We visited the museum two days ago.
questions.explanation: two days ago 是具体过去时间，用一般过去时 visited。
questions.evidence: We visited the museum two days ago.

options: She has just finished her homework.
She has just finish her homework.
She have just finished her homework.
answers: She has just finished her homework.
questions.explanation: just 常与现在完成时连用，表示刚刚完成。主语 She 用 has。
questions.evidence: She has just finished her homework.

options: I have never been to Japan.
I have never go to Japan.
I never have been to Japan.
answers: I have never been to Japan.
questions.explanation: never 常与现在完成时连用，表示从未有过某种经历。
questions.evidence: I have never been to Japan.

options: They have known each other for ten years.
They knew each other for ten years.
They have know each other for ten years.
They are knowing each other for ten years.
answers: They have known each other for ten years.
questions.explanation: for ten years 表示持续一段时间，用现在完成时 have known。know 是状态动词，一般不用进行时。
questions.evidence: They have known each other for ten years.
